physicalEvidence.summary: Full February 5, 2026 ChicGrasp paper §§3.5–4 verifies a UR10e with independently actuated dual-jaw gripper. A conditional diffusion policy trained on100 multiview demonstrations controls Cartesian translation and two jaw commands for grasping. A fixed seven-waypoint routine then performs lift/rehang. The real evaluation reports113/140 complete trials; this is a lab proof of concept, not industrial-speed deployment. University news identifies Wang as project leader and corresponding author, and his current lab roster includes the experiment’s student authors: physical25.

unknowns: Host is University of Arkansas Fayetteville, not UA Little Rock or University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences. Official public contact: dongyiw@uark.edu.

ChicGrasp’s wrist orientation is fixed: the five action dimensions are three translations and two binary jaw states, not five continuous arm pose degrees of freedom. Learned grasping is followed by scripted motion; do not describe the full cycle as end-to-end learned.

The 2026 publisher version uses100 demonstrations and reports80.71% over140 trials. The unrevised May 2025 arXiv version has50 demonstrations and 40.6%; do not mix their experimental numbers. The reported38-second full cycle remains far slower than the cited human pace.

The separate 2026 Koopman swabbing paper uses polynomial/RBF observables and conventional lifted-system control, not a deep-neural controller. It corroborates robotics activity but is not needed for the diffusion-policy claim.
